name: Ilulissat Icefjord
description: On Greenland's west coast, 250 km north of the Arctic Circle, the Ilulissat Icefjord runs 40 km from the ice sheet to Disko Bay, just south of the town of Ilulissat. Its glacier, Sermeq Kujalleq, sheds more than 35 cubic kilometres of ice each year, more than any glacier outside Antarctica. You can watch huge icebergs crack off and drift through the fjord. Scientists have studied the glacier for over 250 years to understand climate change.
